subject.title: Isolated cron consistently fails with "LLM request failed" on model-call-started phase

question: Should isolated cron always create a fresh transcript/session per run, or should it keep the current direct-reset reuse policy and only force a fresh session after consecutive failures?
rationale: The docs promise a new transcript/session id per isolated run, but current main can reuse a fresh session and the latest user report describes cascading failures that a reset policy would address; automation should not pick that compatibility tradeoff alone.

options.title: Align runtime with fresh-run docs
options.body: Make isolated cron create or force a fresh run session after failures while carrying only documented safe preferences and auth overrides.

options.title: Keep reuse and update docs
options.body: Preserve the current direct-reset reuse policy, document when sessions are reused, and add diagnostics so users can intentionally reset stuck cron sessions.

options.title: Defer session policy
options.body: Land only the watchdog fix candidates now and keep this broad issue open for live proof of whether session reuse remains a separate bug.

recommendation.title: Align runtime with fresh-run docs
recommendation.body: Make isolated cron create or force a fresh run session after failures while carrying only documented safe preferences and auth overrides.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent cron timer and docs work plus broader ownership of cron behavior decisions.
